preamble: Under Ehret's reconstruction of Proto-East-Cushitic *tʼ (kept as tʼ in Highland East Cushitic), the northern Lowland East Cushitic languages Somali, Afar and Rendille have the voiced retroflex stop [ɖ] (Somali and Oromo spelling dh). Sasse (1979) instead reconstructs *ɗ and treats Highland tʼ as the innovation, so the direction of change is disputed.

examples.note: Ehret (1991) #147; Oromo dhiiga has the implosive [ɗ].

sources: Ehret, C. (1991). The Consonant Inventory of Proto-Eastern Cushitic. Studies in African Linguistics 22(3), 211–276. https://journals.flvc.org/sal/article/view/107420
Sasse, H.-J. (1979). The Consonant Phonemes of Proto-East-Cushitic (PEC): A First Approximation. Afroasiatic Linguistics 7(1), 1–67.
